sourcedFrom: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year in these books)
cleanIntro: The APX A1 is the one pistol in this group that does NOT need the trigger pulled to come apart: a striker deactivation button drops the striker for you. Press it with a punch or a ballpoint tip, rotate the take down lever, and the slide runs off the front.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber INSPECTED — not assumed
steps.action: Beretta's first field-stripping instruction is to remove the magazine and then look into the chamber. Look, do not feel and do not assume: the take down lever turns on a loaded pistol exactly as it does on an empty one.
steps.aside: WARNING: Make sure the pistol is unloaded. If not, unload it following the instructions in this manual UNLOADING (page 16).
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and ensure the pistol is unloaded by inspecting the barrel’s chamber.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-29

steps.title: ⛔ Striker deactivation button — no trigger pull needed
steps.action: Retract the slide and hold it, then press the striker deactivation button with a small punch or the tip of a ballpoint pen until you hear the click. That click is the striker disengaging. This is the feature that lets an APX come apart without the trigger being pulled, and using it is the safe habit — build it in.
steps.aside: Depress the Striker Deactivation Button with a small punch or the tip of a ballpoint pen.
steps.quote: Retract the slide and hold it
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-29

steps.title: Push, then rotate the take down lever
steps.action: Push the take down lever in and then rotate it. Push first — trying to turn it without pushing is what makes people think it is seized.
steps.quote: Push and then rotate the take down lever.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-29

steps.title: Rotate the takedown lever, then slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Push the takedown lever and rotate it, then run the slide forward and off the frame. Nothing is under tension at this point; the recoil spring comes out in the next step.
steps.prose: ⚠ Beretta's own sentence for the slide coming off cannot be quoted here: the extraction splices a page number inside the word — "and re20 move it from the frame" — so the quote covers the lever, which is intact, and the slide removal is carried in this guide's own words.
steps.quote: Push and then rotate the take down lever.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-29

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then tilt the barrel by its cam lug
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring assembly out of the slide, then grasp the barrel by the cam lug, tilt it and take it out. Four parts on the bench and that is the whole published strip.
steps.quote: Tilt the barrel by grasping the cam lug and remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-29

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, all the way through before pulling back
steps.action: Oil on the bore brush, in from the chamber end, and push it ALL the way through before you draw it back — reversing a brush mid-bore is how bristles get folded over and dragged. Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one emerges clean, then the locking lug, then a light oil everywhere.
steps.aside: Clean the barrel locking lug with a cloth soaked in gun oil. Lightly oil the entire barrel prior to reassembly.
steps.quote: Apply gun oil to a bore-cleaning brush. Insert the brush into the barrel from the chamber end and scrub the chamber and bore thoroughly. Make sure you pass the bore brush all the way through the barrel before pulling back through.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — BARREL

steps.title: Slide: breech face, extractor, rails, locking shoulders
steps.action: Oiled cloth over the slide with attention to the breech face, the extractor, the slide rails and the locking shoulders. NYLON brush only if it needs one — Beretta names the material, and a steel brush on a coated slide is not a small mistake.
steps.quote: Clean the slide with a cloth soaked in gun oil paying particular attention to the breech face, extractor, slide rails, locking shoulders. If necessary, use a NYLON cleaning brush.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — SLIDE

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly and the frame's three named areas
steps.action: Light oil on the spring guide assembly, nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled. On the frame, Beretta names exactly three areas: the cocking lever, the ejector and the slide rails. Dry them, then oil the rails lightly.
steps.aside: Using a cloth lightly soaked in gun oil, clean the areas of the cocking lever, the ejector, and the slide rails.
steps.quote: Lightly oil the spring guide assembly with gun oil. After extensive use it may be necessary to first clean these parts using a NYLON cleaning brush.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — RECOIL SPRING / FRAME

steps.title: ⛔ The magazine goes back DRY
steps.action: The follower must slide down freely under thumb pressure. Dry the internal walls with a cloth and leave NO oil in the magazine — oil in a magazine box collects the dust that eventually stops the follower, and Beretta says so flatly.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Do not apply excess oil. Accumulation of oil attracts dirt and dust, which can interfere with the functioning and reliability of the firearm.
steps.quote: Make sure the magazine is thoroughly clean and that the follower slides easily downward if pressed. Dry the internal walls of the magazine box with a cloth. Do not leave any oil in the magazine.
steps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — MAGAZINE

deepSteps.title: Beretta publishes the chassis removal — memorise before you move
deepSteps.action: The APX A1's serialised part is the chassis, and Beretta publishes how to take it out of the polymer frame for maintenance or replacement. It starts from a completed field strip, and the book's own instruction before anything moves is to LOOK at how the components sit — this is a job where the order of reassembly is not obvious afterwards.
deepSteps.aside: CAUTION: Before proceeding with the disassembly of the parts, closely observe and memorize the position of the components to make assembly easier.
deepSteps.quote: Field strip the pistol following the FIELD STRIPPING (page 28) instructions in this manual to remove the slide assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Take down lever horizontal, then out right-to-left
deepSteps.action: Rotate the take down lever to HORIZONTAL and push it out from right to left. Set it aside where it cannot roll off the bench — it is a small part and the pistol does not reassemble without it.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the take down lever to a horizontal position and push it out from right to left and place it aside.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Cocking lever spring leg lifted, THEN the rear chassis pin
deepSteps.action: This is a two-punch job and the order matters. With a small punch, lift the cocking lever spring leg out of its retaining groove in the rear chassis pin. Keep it lifted with that punch and use a SECOND punch to drive the pin out right to left. Try to push the pin with the spring leg still in the groove and you will bend the leg.
deepSteps.quote: Keeping the leg of the spring lifted and using a second punch, push from right to left the rear chassis pin out of the frame.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Chassis lifts out only while the striker button is depressed
deepSteps.action: The chassis will not come out until the striker deactivation button is pressed in far enough for the tip of its pin to clear the inner walls of the frame. Punch or ballpoint tip on the button, lift, and it comes free.
deepSteps.quote: When attempting to lift the chassis out of the frame depress the striker deactivation button with a small punch or the tip of a ballpoint pen. When the tip of the pin clears the inner walls of the frame the chassis will lift out.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Back in: front corner first, and listen for the snap
deepSteps.action: Start the chassis in at the FRONT corner and roll the rear down until the striker deactivation button touches the top of the frame. Press lightly on the chassis while depressing that button with a punch, and it drops in with an audible snap. Then the rear chassis pin, then the spring-leg check, then the take down lever back through left to right and rotated vertical.
deepSteps.aside: Check that the cocking lever spring leg has engaged the groove of the pin
deepSteps.quote: There will be an audible “snap” when the chassis is seated.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX A1 User Manual — MAN0011 01 (form code printed in the running header) — FRAME INSTALLATION, printed p.38

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush in from the CHAMBER end and all the way through before pulling back
Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one comes out clean
⛔ Never clean the barrel with the pistol assembled
Light oil on the whole barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Cloth or nylon brush on the breech face, extractor, rails and locking shoulders
Dry the slide surfaces, then lightly oil the guides

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Light gun oil on the spring guide assembly
Nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled — never a steel one

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Fouling off the frame rails and the magazine well
Magazine lips and follower cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first: tilt it, muzzle end through the hole in the front of the slide, then lower the rear end into position.
Recoil spring assembly in with the large flat end engaged in the recess of the barrel cam lug.
⛔ Check the takedown control is in its UNLOCKED position before the slide goes on.
Slide assembly onto the frame, then retract it slowly with the muzzle in a safe direction and CONFIRM the takedown control has returned to LOCKED.
Function check the striker deactivation button and the trigger safety before loading.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: check the take down lever sits vertical, then retract the slide with the muzzle safe and watch the lever rotate and shift to LOCKED. Cycle the slide several times, confirm it returns fully to battery, and check the trigger safety blade returns. ⛔ Do not release a slide under spring pressure with the lever unlocked — Beretta's own caution is that the slide can leave the frame.
